Coping today: group chats, a shared spreadsheet, mental checklists.

Cost: their own time and stress, plus real trip failures — forgotten gear, no-shows, awkward money fights afterward.

First move this week: post in 2-3 of these asking how people split costs and gear for group trips, then DM the 10-15 people with the roughest stories and invite them to try Campfire Tab on their next trip.

Does one of these feel like the right hunting ground, or do you already know where your organizers hang out?

Here's a first pass — take it as a draft, not gospel.

Beachhead: recreational friend-group organizers who camp 2+ times a year with a rotating crew of 4-8 people (not solo backpackers, not families with a fixed roster). That's a meaningful slice of the ~40-50M Americans who camp annually, though most of that group never plans anything beyond a text thread.

Who's already serving pieces of this:
1. Splitwise — cost-splitting, but no gear or trip context
2. Google Sheets / Notion — free, flexible, but manual and easy to abandon
3. Venmo — settles money after the fact, doesn't prevent the fight
4. PackPoint / Gaia GPS — packing lists or route planning, not group coordination

None of them fuse gear claiming + cost splitting + trip logistics into one flow — which is your opening. So here's the sharp one: if a determined organizer can already stitch together Splitwise + a shared sheet + Venmo for free, what makes Campfire Tab worth switching to instead of just gluing those together?

Here's a first pass.

Core mechanism: the host answers a few AI-guided questions about the trip (headcount, duration, activities), the AI builds a shared gear/task board plus a cost split, and group members claim items and see what they owe — replacing the scattered texts and chasing.

V1 should probably be: AI-generated gear/task board, item claiming, automatic even-split cost tracking, and the email confirmation of what each person's on the hook for. Out of v1: actual in-app payment processing (Venmo-style money movement), route/itinerary planning, and weather or packing-list intelligence beyond gear.

The thing I'm least sure about: does Campfire Tab need to move money itself, or is it enough to just track who owes what and let people settle up however they already do?

Here are four directions, each with a different personality:

1. Campfire Tab — the shared tab that keeps every camping trip fair
2. Basecamp Split — split gear, cost, and chaos before you even pitch a tent
3. Trailmates — the app that keeps your group from falling apart in the woods
4. Packlist — one board for everything your trip needs, claimed and covered

Which of these feels closest to what you're picturing?

Here's a first pass: the organizer is the one feeling the pain and driving adoption, so they're the natural payer — the group members are unlikely to install anything just to pay their share. Shape-wise, freemium fits the occasional-use pattern: free gear board and cost-splitting for everyone, with a paid upgrade for the AI-generated onboarding and checklist emails that make it feel effortless. Roughly $4-6/month if they organize often, or a one-time $9-15 per-trip fee if trips are rare — either could work depending on how frequently your organizer actually plans.
